title: Get Started with glyanno
text: Mass spectrometry-based glycomics glycoproteomics often yield data limited structural resolution. example, MALDI-TOF MS-based glycomics typically provides m/z values, many LC-MS/MS-based glycoproteomics workflows identify basic glycan compositions lack isomer specificity. Mass spectrometry alone frequently fails distinguish specific monosaccharide isomers (e.g., differentiating Mannose Galactose), resolve linkage details (e.g., a1-3 vs b1-4). theory, full structural resolution achievable combining MS orthogonal techniques enzymatic digestion NMR; however, approaches often resource-intensive time-consuming. Unfortunately, advanced downstream analyses—glycan biosynthetic pathway reconstruction offered glyenzy— require fully resolved glycan structures, including specific monosaccharide identities linkage information.

title: Get Started with glyanno
text: glyanno bridges gap. package designed maximize utility mass spectrometry data annotating probable biological context derived knowledge bases. package features four core functions: mz_to_comp(): Identifies possible glycan compositions m/z values. comp_to_struc(): Maps glycan compositions potential glycan structures. enhance_comp(): Refines generic glycan compositions concrete, monosaccharide-specific compositions. enhance_struc(): Resolves low-resolution glycan structures high-resolution structures linkage information.  Note: package relies glyrepr glydb. recommend familiarizing packages, especially glyrepr, using glyanno. Additionally, basic understanding IUPAC-condensed notation recommended vignette. can refer tutorial.
code: library(glyanno) library(glydb) #> Loading required package: glyrepr

title: Get Started with glyanno
text: Let’s demonstrate functions step--step, starting single m/z value. returns every composition glydb matching m/z 406.1325. practice, returning “” possibilities can overwhelming; often want constrain search space based biological context. glydb provides helper functions filter database. example, might want limit search human O-GalNAc glycans. my_db simply glyrepr::glycan_composition() vector. can pass db argument mz_to_comp() filter results. results now significantly relevant specific context. composition identified, can proceed determine potential structures. m/z value 406.1325 corresponds composition Gal(1)GalNAc(1). possible structures composition? Note use glydb_structures() instead glydb_compositions() create structure-specific database. Two structures possible, one Core 1, Core 5. Sometimes just want “possible” result. case, can set return_best TRUE: Core 1 common Core 5, kept. function keeps structure citations multiple matches. Note return_best = TRUE, function returns vector length input instead tibble. glycan matches, <NA> corresponding position. Note functions glyanno works vectorizedly: set return_best TRUE, function directly returns vector: vector always length input, NA glycans match.

Glc(1)GlcNAc(1) #> 4  406. Man(1)GlcNAc(1) my_db <- glydb_compositions(species = "Homo sapiens", glycan_type = "O-GalNAc") my_db #> <glycan_composition[124]> #> [1] Gal(1)GalNAc(1) #> [2] Gal(1)GlcNAc(1)GalNAc(1) #> [3] GlcNAc(1)GalNAc(1) #> [4] GlcNAc(2)GalNAc(1) #> [5] GalNAc(2) #> [6] Gal(2)GlcNAc(1)GalNAc(1)Neu5Ac(1) #> [7] Gal(1)GalNAc(2)Neu5Ac(2) #> [8] Gal(1)GalNAc(1)Fuc(1) #> [9] Gal(2)GlcNAc(2)GalNAc(2)Fuc(1) #> [10] Gal(2)GlcNAc(1)GalNAc(1) #> ... Gal(1)GalNAc(1) struc_db <- glydb_structures(species = "Homo sapiens", glycan_type = "O-GalNAc") comp_to_struc("Gal(1)GalNAc(1)", db = struc_db) #> # A tibble: 2 × 2 #>   composition     structure           #>   <comp>          <struct>            #> 1 Gal(1)GalNAc(1) Gal(b1-3)GalNAc(a1- #> 2 Gal(1)GalNAc(1) Gal(a1-3)GalNAc(a1- comp_to_struc("Gal(1)GalNAc(1)", db = struc_db, return_best = TRUE) #> <glycan_structure[1]> #> [1] Gal(b1-3)GalNAc(a1- #> # Unique structures: 1 comp_to_struc(c("Gal(1)GalNAc(1)", "GlcNAc(1)GalNAc(1)"), db = struc_db, return_best = TRUE) #> <glycan_structure[2]> #> [1] Gal(b1-3)GalNAc(a1- #> [2] GlcNAc(b1-3)GalNAc(a1- #> # Unique structures: 2 comp_to_struc(c("Gal(1)GalNAc(1)", "GlcNAc(1)GalNAc(1)"), db = struc_db, return_best = TRUE) #> <glycan_structure[2]> #> [1] Gal(b1-3)GalNAc(a1- #> [2] GlcNAc(b1-3)GalNAc(a1- #> # Unique structures: 2

title: Hierarchical Glycan Annotation
text: goal glyanno enhance level information resolution glycans hierarchical annotation approach. Starting molecule mass, glyanno calculates possible glycan compositions. Given glycan composition, glyanno deduces possible glycan structures. glycan structures generic monosaccharides (e.g., “Hex”, “HexNAc”), glyanno refines specific types (e.g., “Glc”, “Gal”). structures lacking linkage information (e.g., “Gal(??-?)GalNAc(??-”), glyanno infers likely linkages (e.g., “Gal(b1-3)GalNAc(a1-”).

what: Calculate m/z values of glycans — calculate_mz
title: Calculate m/z values of glycans — calculate_mz
text: function calculates m/z values glycans. Different adducts, mass types, derivatives supported. Custom mass dictionaries also supported.

title: Calculate m/z values of glycans — calculate_mz
code: calculate_mz(glycans, charge = 1, adduct = "H+", mass_dict = NULL, safe = TRUE)

title: Calculate m/z values of glycans — calculate_mz
text: glycans Glycans calculate m/z values . Valid inputs include: glyrepr::glycan_structure() vector. glyrepr::glycan_composition() vector. Byonic style composition strings (e.g. Hex(5)HexNAc(2)). Simple style composition strings (e.g. H5N4F1S1). structure strings supported glyparse::auto_parse(). charge Charge use. Can 0, 1, 2, 3, -1, -2, -3, etc. 0 means neutral. Default 1. adduct Adduct use. Can "H+", "K+", "Na+", "NH4+", "H-", "Cl-", "HCO3-". Default "H+". charge 0, adduct ignored. charge positive, adduct can "H+", "K+", "Na+", "NH4+". charge negative, adduct can "H-", "Cl-", "HCO3-". mass_dict named numeric vector mass monosaccharide residue. Default glyanno_mass_dict(deriv = "none", mass_type = "mono"). custom mass dictionary provided, please make sure names vector names glyanno_mass_dict(). safe Whether raise error unsupported monosaccharides substituents found. TRUE (default), error raised. FALSE, warning raised m/z values invalid glycans set NA.

title: Calculate m/z values of glycans — calculate_mz
text: numeric vector m/z values.

title: Calculate m/z values of glycans — calculate_mz
code: library(glyrepr)  # Different input types calculate_mz(glycan_composition(c(Gal = 1, GalNAc = 1)), charge = 0) #> [1] 383.1428 calculate_mz("Gal(1)GalNAc(1)", charge = 0) #> [1] 383.1428 calculate_mz(as_glycan_structure("Gal(b1-3)GalNAc(a1-"), charge = 0) #> [1] 383.1428 calculate_mz("Gal(b1-3)GalNAc(a1-", charge = 0) #> [1] 383.1428  # For common situation in MALDI-TOF MS calculate_mz("Man(5)GlcNAc(2)", charge = 1,adduct = "Na+") #> [1] 1257.423  # For common situation in ESI MS calculate_mz("Man(5)GlcNAc(2)", charge = 1, adduct = "H+") #> [1] 1235.441  # Calculate permethylated m/z values calculate_mz("Man(5)GlcNAc(2)", charge = 0, mass_dict = glyanno_mass_dict(deriv = "permethyl")) #> [1] 1556.793  # Calculate average mass calculate_mz("Man(5)GlcNAc(2)", charge = 0, mass_dict = glyanno_mass_dict(mass_type = "average")) #> [1] 1235.117  # Vectorization calculate_mz(c("Man(5)GlcNAc(2)", "Gal(1)GalNAc(1)"), charge = 1, adduct = "Na+") #> [1] 1257.4231  406.1325

title: Convert glycan composition to glycan structure — comp_to_struc
text: comps Glycan compositions match . Can either: glyrepr::glycan_composition() vector. Byonic style composition strings (e.g. Hex(5)HexNAc(2)). Simple style composition strings (e.g. H5N4F1S1). db Glycan structures match . Can glyrepr::glycan_structure() vector structure strings supported glyparse::auto_parse(). provided, glydb::glydb_structures(structure_level = "intact") used. return_best TRUE, return highest confidence match composition. Requires db confidence attribute. Use glydb::glydb_structures() db enable feature. Default FALSE.

title: Convert glycan composition to glycan structure — comp_to_struc
text: return_best=TRUE: glyrepr::glycan_structure() vector length comps. Unmatched compositions returned NA. return_best=FALSE: tibble following columns: composition: glycan compositions, glyrepr::glycan_composition() vector. structure: possible glycan structures, glyrepr::glycan_structure() vector. Note one glycan composition can multiple rows result, corresponding different possible glycan structures.

title: Convert glycan composition to glycan structure — comp_to_struc
text: db parameter important functions package. default, uses available glycans glydb package, usually larger need. can use helper functions glydb narrow database, e.g. glydb::glydb_compositions() glydb::glydb_structures(). can use species glycan_type parameters focus specific species glycan type. example, interested N-glycan compositions human, can use glydb::glydb_compositions(species = "Homo sapiens", glycan_type = "N"). Also, can decide level information database setting mono_type glydb::glydb_compositions() structure_level glydb::glydb_structures(). can pass result db parameter function. example,
code: my_db <- glydb::glydb_compositions(species = "Homo sapiens", glycan_type = "N") mz_to_comp(mz, db = my_db)

title: glyanno: Hierarchical Glycan Annotation — glyanno-package
text: Hierarchical annotation glycans based molecule mass, composition, structure. Starting molecule mass, glyanno calculates possible glycan compositions. Given glycan composition, glyanno deduces possible glycan structures. glycan structures generic monosaccharides (e.g., "Hex", "HexNAc"), glyanno refines specific types (e.g., "Glc", "Gal"). structures lacking linkage information (e.g., "Gal(??-?)GalNAc(??-"), glyanno infers likely linkages (e.g., "Gal(b1-3)GalNAc(a1-").
